title: Fallback economics + regional preference optimizer (heuristics + spreadsheet)
body:
Purpose

This doc captures a working draft of a lightweight cost model and heuristic rules for a region-aware fallback policy. The goal is to produce an operationally simple policy that: (1) meets latency SLOs, (2) minimizes expected per-token cost, and (3) degrades gracefully when preferred capacity (spot/on-demand/reserved) is unavailable.

Quick summary / thesis
- Treat routing decisions as a triage: prefer cheapest compatible capacity that meets SLO + interruption tolerance.
- Add a small region-preference penalty to reflect egress/latency/regulatory overheads.
- Model expected cost as a combination of steady-state hourly cost and probability-weighted fallback costs (including preemption, cross-region egress, and cold-start latency cost).

Assumptions and inputs (spreadsheet tabs)
- Inputs tab: per-region per-instance pricing (on-demand, spot, reserved amortized), estimated average throughput per instance (tokens/sec), average sequence length (tokens/request), latency SLO (ms P95), spot interruption rate per hour, cross-region egress per-MB price.
- Workload tab: distribution of request sizes, peak:baseline ratio, %latency-sensitive calls.
- Policy-sim tab: simulate routing decisions over an hour of traffic, sample preemptions, calculate weighted cost and SLA misses.

Baseline numeric assumptions (editable in sheet)
- Throughput per GPU: 200 tokens/sec (avg for targeted model at production batch sizes).
- Tokens per hour per GPU = 200 * 3600 = 720,000 tokens/hr.
- On-demand hourly: US-WEST = $3.60/hr, US-EAST = $3.80/hr.
- Spot hourly: US-WEST = $0.95/hr (preemption ~8%/hr), US-EAST spot = $1.05/hr (preemption ~10%/hr).
- Reserved effective hourly = $2.40/hr (amortized commit).
- Cross-region egress cost: $0.09 per GB (~0.00009 per token assuming 1 token ~= 0.3 KB — adjust).

Simple cost-per-1M-tokens back-of-envelope (tab: quick-calc)
- Tokens/hr = 720k. Multipliers: 1M / 720k = 1.3889.
- On-demand US-WEST: $3.60 * 1.3889 ≈ $5.00 per 1M tokens.
- Spot US-WEST: $0.95 * 1.3889 ≈ $1.32 per 1M tokens.
- Reserved: $2.40 * 1.3889 ≈ $3.33 per 1M tokens.

Modeling preemption/fallback costs
- If a spot instance is preempted, we assume: (a) lost in-flight tokens (small) and (b) routing to fallback capacity (secondary region or on-demand) with a cold-start latency penalty for warmup and possibly additional egress cost if cross-region.
- Define preemption penalty as: P(preempt) * (delta_cost + SLA_penalty_cost).
  - Example: P=8% --> expected additional cost = 0.08 * (cost difference between destination and source) + latency_penalty.
- Latency_penalty: convert expected SLA miss to dollar-equivalent using product/business metric (e.g., $0.07 per missed request for revenue-impacting endpoints).

Fallback tiers (policy suggestion)
- Tier 0 (preferred): local spot (if latency-sensitive flag = false and model meets throughput)
- Tier 1 (preferred-failover): local reserved / on-demand (if spot preempted or if latency-sensitive)
- Tier 2 (cross-region): nearest region spot/reserved if Tier1 capacity exhausted (incurs egress penalty + additional latency)
- Tier 3 (graceful degrade): cheaper lower-capability model variant in same region (quantized model) to preserve availability at reduced quality

Heuristic routing score (single scalar to rank candidates)
- Score = cost_score * (1 + region_penalty) + alpha * expected_preemption_cost + beta * latency_risk_score
  - cost_score = hourly_cost / baseline_throughput (converted to $/1M tokens in sheet)
  - region_penalty = 0.0 for same-region; 0.08 for cross-region (tunable)
  - expected_preemption_cost = preempt_rate * (cost_delta + SLA_penalty_dollars)
  - latency_risk_score = normalized probability of missing P95 under current queueing (0..1) * SLA_cost_multiplier
  - alpha, beta are knobs exposed in console (default alpha=1.0, beta=2.0 for latency-sensitive routes)

Spreadsheet layout (recommended tabs)
- inputs | pricing_by_region | workload | policy_params | model_perf (throughput/latency by batch/seq_len) | sim_results | sensitivity_outputs | notes

Example scenario (1M tokens over hour, mostly small requests)
- Preferred: US-WEST spot => expected cost = $1.32 per 1M tokens.
- If spot preemption occurs 8% of the time and fallback is on-demand local: additional expected cost = 0.08 * (5.00 - 1.32) = $0.30 per 1M tokens.
- Total expected cost ≈ $1.62 per 1M tokens (plus tiny egress/cold-start costs).
- If fallback is cross-region on-demand (egress + latency): add egress ~$0.05 and latency-equivalent penalty $0.20 => total ≈ $2.07 per 1M tokens.

Sensitivity notes (things to watch in the model)
- Throughput variance (tokens/sec) has outsized effect: if real throughput is 150 tps vs 200 tps, cost per 1M tokens jumps ~33%.
- Preemption rate estimation must be per-hour and per-instance-type; real cloud markets show spikes in preemption probability during maintenance windows — model should allow time-of-day weighting.
- Cold-start latency and the size of warmup KV cache matter for cost of fallback.

Operational metrics to produce after rollout
- Expected cost per 1M tokens by route and realized cost (actual billing vs model)
- Preemption events/sec and % requests rerouted to fallback per route
- P95 latency per route and % of requests incurring cross-region egress
- Quality regressions if using quantized fallback models (tracked via eval prompt set)

Open questions / TODOs
- How to convert latency SLA misses to $ reliably across product lines? Ask growth/customer-metrics for per-request dollar loss estimates.
- Should we expose alpha/beta knobs directly to customers or keep them internal and surface simple toggles (cost-priority / latency-priority)?
- Need to instrument per-request tagging for route chosen and whether request experienced fallback; add to tracing plan.
- Add support for time-of-day preemption profiles in spreadsheet (tab: preempt_profile).

Action items (short-term)
- [Aisha] finish populating pricing_by_region with latest cloud quotes (ETA: 2024-11-25).
- [Liam] add model_perf numbers for v2-small and v2-quantized by 2024-12-01.
- [Marcelo] hookup sim_runs to Jupyter / GitHub actions to produce nightly sensitivity_outputs (ETA: 2025-01-02).

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Might want a fallback budget cap: e.g., allow up to X% of traffic to cross-region before triggering a policy that restricts spot usage.
- Consider a holdback pool of reserved capacity that we only consume on cross-region fallback to avoid egress churn.

Unresolved / friction points
- Cross-region regulatory constraints for certain customers (cannot route out of eu-west) — policy must honor customer level constraints.
- Measuring true egress per token is noisy (depends on compression, chunking). Keep a 10% safety margin in egress estimate.

Appendix: quick cheat-sheet of knobs in console
- cost_weight (0..10): higher = more cost sensitive
- latency_weight (0..10): higher = more latency-sensitive routes choose on-demand/reserved more often
- region_penalty_map: per-region small penalty to reflect egress/latency/regulatory cost
- fallback_budget_pct: percent of traffic allowed to fallback cross-region per hour

End notes
- This is a working doc — spreadsheet linked above (opt-routing-cost-model-v4) has live cells and scenario toggles. Keep the model simple: we can iterate on simulation fidelity after we validate initial assumptions with real billing data.

-- Aisha
